title: States Weekly: November 4, 2026
text:
States Weekly: November 4, 2026

Photo: Mavlers

Newsletter
by

Aryan D’Rozario

Published November 4, 2026

Big News: Tamil Nadu introduces a Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Policy; Goa approves the Chief Minister’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Innovation Scheme, 2026; Bihar approves the Bihar Artificial Intelligence Policy, 2026; Karnataka announces the Karnataka State Regional Urbanization Plan 2047 (KSRUP 2047); Maharashtra amends its Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Policy 2026; and more.Health Haryana expands its Chirayu-Ayushman Haryana Healthcare Scheme. The scheme has been broadened to include middle-income families who earn more than $3100 (INR 3 lakh) annually.Source: TribuneIn detail: Press ReleaseClimate Change and EnergyDelhi passes the DERC (Terms and Conditions for Green Energy Open Access) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2026. The regulations, passed by the Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission (DERC) relax norms for commercial and industrial consumers seeking to source renewable energy. Under the revised regulations, consumers will no longer be required to be connected at 11 kV or above to procure renewable energy through open access mechanisms.Source: Times of IndiaIn detail: Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions for Green Energy Open Access) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2026Haryana suspends the implementation of a 25-year electricity distribution license granted to Eleven Power (EEPL). The license covered the districts of Gurugram and Nuh.Source: EnergeticaIn detail: HERC OrderTamil Nadu introduces a Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Policy. The policy targets the deployment of at least 2.5 GW or 10 GWh of energy storage capacity over the next three years and establishes a framework for developing both standalone battery storage installations and co-located storage systems integrated with renewable energy projects.Source: Solar QuarterIn detail: Tamil Nadu Battery Energy Storage Systems Policy, 2026Maharashtra waives the 25 percent transfer fee on land acquired for renewable energy projects. The fee will no longer be charged when land moves from a parent company to its subsidiary.Source: Economic TimesIn detail: Exemption of Transfer FeesFinanceNothing critical to report this week.Industrial Policy and Business RegulationsGoa approves the Chief Minister’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Innovation Scheme, 2026. The scheme aims to promote innovation in the MSME sector and extend incentives under the Start-Up Policy to registered MSMEs.Source: Times of IndiaBihar approves a Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Policy, 2026. The policy aims to create 10 million direct and indirect jobs over five years, raise the state’s credit-deposit ratio to 75 percent, and set up an MSME cluster and center in each of Bihar’s 38 districts.Source: ETVIn detail: Cabinet DecisionsBihar approves the Bihar Artificial Intelligence Policy, 2026. The policy aims to develop the state into an attractive and competitive destination for AI companies, startups, and digital enterprises.Source: ETVIn detail: Cabinet DecisionsLand Acquisition and Labor Regulations Labor Regulations  Tamil Nadu allows local bodies to approve residential and commercial building plans. Under provisions issued by the Housing and Urban Development Department, corporations and municipalities can approve residential buildings with a floor space index (FSI) area of up to 1,500 square meters, equivalent to approximately 16,140 square feet.Source: Prop News TimeIn detail: Press ReleaseTamil Nadu amends the Tamil Nadu Combined Development and Building Rules, 2019. The new rules raise the maximum permissible height for specified non-high-rise buildings from 60 feet to 64 feet. The changes also ease parking requirements for offices, revise commercial land-use provisions along wider roads, and expand the range of developments permitted in Chennai’s restricted aquifer recharge area.Source: Hindustan TimesIn detail: Government OrderInfrastructure and GovernanceKarnataka announces the Karnataka State Regional Urbanization Plan 2047 (KSRUP 2047). The 20-year plan aims to develop cities and towns across the state, reducing dependence on Bengaluru as the primary growth center. The plan envisages more than 50 initiatives across seven pillars, with an estimated investment of $52.66 billion (INR 5 lakh crore).Source: Money ControlMadhya Pradesh announces a 2 percent increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for state government employees and officers, as well as pensioners.Source: Money ControlMaharashtra amends its Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Policy 2026. The amendments aim to simplify infrastructure project approvals, reduce administrative delays, and improve coordination among government departments.Source: The Hans IndiaMaharashtra approves $789.9 million (INR 7,500 crore) in drought aid for farmers before Diwali. About 15 million eligible farmers in 304 drought-hit areas will each receive an advance payment of $52.66 (INR 5,000).Source: New Indian ExpressIn detail: Government Notification (in Marathi)Tamil Nadu announces a 3 percent increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for state government employees, teachers, pensioners, and family pensioners.Source: New Indian ExpressIn detail: Press Release (in Tamil)Telangana approves the Telangana Gram Panchayat (Village Council) Comprehensive Development Plan (GPSAP) Rules, 2026. The rules make it mandatory for all gram panchayats to prepare integrated development plans covering infrastructure, employment, housing, livelihoods, and welfare programs.Source: The HinduIn detail: Telangana GPSAP-2026Chhattisgarh announces a 2 percent increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for state government employees, teachers, pensioners, and family pensioners.Source: Times of IndiaJammu and Kashmir approves the Jammu and Kashmir Combined Competitive Services (Probation and Examination) Rules, 2026. The rules govern the probation of officers recruited through Jammu and Kashmir’s combined competitive exam, including the length of probation, the training and departmental exams officers must pass, and the conditions for confirming them in service.Source: Kashmir LifeIn detail: Jammu and Kashmir Combined Competitive Services (Probation and Examination) Rules, 2026Keralam passes the Keralam Senior Citizens’ (Care and Protection of Rights) Bill, 2026. The bill sets up state and district bodies to monitor care homes and investigate abuse, and penalizes elder abuse, property grabbing, and unregistered care homes.Source: The HinduIn detail: Keralam Senior Citizens’ (Care and Protection of Rights) Bill, 2026Water and SanitationGoa approves new Water and Air Pollution Control Rules. The rules introduce fee concessions for micro, small and medium enterprises, simplified consent procedures, and online applications.Source: Digital GoaIn detail: Goa Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) RulesCenter – State RelationsThe Union government approves the Lakshadweep Tourism Trade (Registration, Safety and Facilitation) Regulations, 2026. The regulations mandate official registration for service providers, strict safety protocols, and severe penalties for any damage to the fragile marine ecosystem.Source: Deccan ChronicleIn detail: Lakshadweep Tourism Trade (Registration, Safety and Facilitation) Regulation, 2026Any OtherWest Bengal bars future School Service Commission-appointed school teachers from direct politics. The cabinet-approved rule covers new teachers in government-aided and government-sponsored schools and exempts current teachers serving as elected local body representatives.Source: New Indian ExpressGoa orders source certificates for all live poultry entering the state. The Directorate of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services will deny entry to consignments without them, a measure aimed at compliance with animal transport rules.Source: Goan
